channel.title: Rochdale Daily
channel.description: Independent local news, public-service information and reporting from Rochdale borough.

item.title: Ten years without answers: the continuing search for Rochdale’s Jack Stewart
item.description: Jack Stewart vanished from Spotland on 8 February 2016. His missing-person appeal remains listed a decade later. Here are the original clothing details, what the community did, and how to report information safely.

item.title: 651 SEWAGE SPILLS INTO THE RIVER ROCH: 3,271 HOURS OF DISCHARGES — WHAT IS IN OUR WATER AND WHO PAYS?
item.description: Seventeen outlets discharged into the River Roch in 2025. Rochdale Daily examines what residents and wildlife may be exposed to, how water is tested, why storm overflows operate, and which fines have actually been imposed.

item.title: FIVE YEARS LATER, A COURT SUMMONS: Rochdale residents report historic Council Tax demands as arrears reach £28.4m
item.description: Several residents tell Rochdale Daily they have received summonses for old Council Tax bills, including a 2021 account. With arrears reportedly £28.4m, we examine recovery rules, compare council finances, and list free debt help.

item.title: BREAKING INVESTIGATION: £50.3m owed by Rochdale Council companies as £19.5m Council Tax shortfall raises scrutiny
item.description: Rochdale's draft accounts show £50.309m in Upperbanks company loan balances, £2.02m interest added and only £132,000 repaid in 2025/26. We examine the figures, the 2022 decisions and the councillors responsible for oversight.

item.title: Halloween in Rochdale 2026: parties, pumpkins and spooky events across the borough
item.description: 39 dated Halloween listings across Rochdale, Heywood, Middleton, Milnrow, Littleborough, Norden and Wardle, with prices, times, age suitability, venues and booking links.

item.title: East Middleton councillor questions parking charge warning after petrol station breakdown
item.description: Labour councillor Georgina Jacques says she was warned about a parking charge while waiting for the RAC after her car broke down on Oldham Road.

item.title: A kitchen to be proud of this Christmas: meet Rochdale’s family-run SJF Granite & Quartz
item.description: With 25 years of experience and a reported 124 five-star reviews, this local family business puts craftsmanship and personal service at the heart of its work.

item.title: Pacific, Mangos and Empire until morning: remembering Rochdale’s strip
item.description: Box-dye red hair, Jägerbombs and taxi queues that lasted hours—remembering Rochdale’s strip, its familiar faces and the venues keeping the town alive today.

item.title: Hillcrest Road, roadworks in Rochdale from 26 October 2026
item.description: Rochdale Borough Council lists work affecting Hillcrest Road in Rochdale; expected timings: 12midnight, Monday, 26 October 2026–11.59pm, Friday, 30 October 2026..

item.title: Bamford and Norden’s 450-home allocation: housing choice versus pressure on green space
item.description: The Bamford and Norden allocation envisages around 450 homes alongside improvements to sports and recreation facilities. Its development framework promotes family and affordable housing, but a framework does not establish a completed scheme, a housebuilder’s final layout or an affordable tenancy.

item.title: College Bank’s future remains a housing question as residents move from the Seven Sisters
item.description: College Bank’s future cannot yet be presented as a confirmed number of new homes. RBH’s July 2026 update records that 100 customers had accepted offers of another home and 64 had moved from the high-rise blocks at that point.

item.title: Crimble Mill’s housing plans must balance heritage rescue with the cost to local families
item.description: Crimble Mill’s detailed scheme is 214 homes: 33 apartments in the mill, 31 houses in the existing complex and 150 houses on neighbouring greenfield land. The broader 250-home allocation is not a second development or the approved detailed count.

item.title: Foundry Fields approval includes only five reported social-rent homes among 199 houses
item.description: Taylor Wimpey’s Foundry Fields scheme received a reported six-to-four committee vote in favour, with one abstention, in January 2026. The 199-home proposal includes detached, semi-detached and terraced houses, with five reported social-rented properties.

item.title: Castleton Sidings brings 191 homes, with discounted ownership and rail land in the package
item.description: Hawks View is a 191-home development on the former Castleton Sidings site. Kellen’s current partnership page identifies 162 market homes, ten First Homes and 19 affordable homes with Mosscare St Vincent. The rental/ownership split within those 19 remains unspecified.

item.title: Littleborough’s former AkzoNobel site shows how brownfield housing can include discounted ownership
item.description: The former AkzoNobel site was announced as a 126-home development through Countryside Partnerships and Together Housing. Its original tenure package included 14 shared-ownership homes and five First Homes, with open-market housing sold under the Bovis brand.

item.title: Hollingworth Road’s 309 homes: the school land promise needs a delivery explanation
item.description: Bloor’s Hollingworth Road scheme has been reduced from 312 to 309 homes. Council reporting in June 2026 records site preparation. Developer material includes a central green corridor, sustainable drainage, walking and cycling links and land for a primary school.

item.title: Holtwood Green’s 56 homes include eight announced First Homes in Middleton
item.description: Duchy Homes’ Holtwood Green scheme comprises 56 homes on Manchester Old Road. The developer announced eight homes under the First Homes scheme, approximately 14.3% of the total, alongside a three- to five-bedroom market offer.

item.title: Lower Falinge’s proposed 270 homes would replace 150: what residents gain and lose
item.description: RBH’s next Lower Falinge phase is reported to envisage 270 affordable-rented homes across two parcels, replacing 150 homes proposed for demolition. If implemented on that basis, the eventual net addition is around 120 homes, not 270.

item.title: Newhey Quarry’s 250-home allocation needs a clearer account of remediation and affordability
item.description: Newhey Quarry is allocated for around 250 homes, with additional parking intended to support the nearby tram stop. The council’s land assessment classifies the site as brownfield, but the quarry’s history makes its treatment more complicated than simply describing it as unused land.

item.title: Northstone’s 186-home Heywood phase advances, but household costs remain unclear
item.description: Northstone’s Hareshill Road phase has moved beyond its earlier promotion for up to 190 homes. The council’s June 2026 development update records planning approval for 186. That distinction matters when residents compare publicity with the scheme that will actually be built.

item.title: Parkfield House redevelopment brings 20 homes and an 80-bed care home to Middleton
item.description: Muller Property Group says it has secured approval for 20 townhouses and an 80-bed care home at the former Parkfield House site off Manchester Old Road. The scheme reuses a three-acre brownfield site and involves demolition of the former Chubb Locks headquarters.

item.title: Kirkholt’s Queen’s Drive scheme promises 28 social-rented homes
item.description: A 28-home scheme off Queen’s Drive is reported as approved for Mosscare St Vincent Housing. It comprises 23 one-bedroom apartments and five four-bedroom terraced houses, all intended for social rent.

item.title: Where Rochdale’s next homes are planned—and who can afford them
item.description: Our investigation examines 22 housing developments and regeneration plans across Rochdale borough: homes, prices, affordable tenure, land, school places, GP capacity and transport funding.

item.title: Rochdale station’s 33 new flats are for private rent: what will tenants actually pay?
item.description: The Corner Plot scheme near Rochdale station will provide 33 one- and two-bedroom apartments for private rent. Oak Construction Projects is carrying out the build, with Mansell Building Solutions appointed for the specialist frame package.

item.title: Silver Hill Manor’s 57 market homes have no affordable provision following viability review
item.description: Silver Hill Manor is a 57-dwelling scheme associated with David Wilson Homes and Rexel Property Group. It combines new housing with refurbishment of the Grade II-listed Silver Hill Farmhouse.

item.title: Simister and Bowlee’s cross-border plan includes 200 homes in Rochdale, not 1,550
item.description: Simister and Bowlee’s housing programme crosses the borough boundary. Bury Council identifies 1,550 homes overall, of which 200 would be in Rochdale. Only the Rochdale share belongs in a total of this borough’s new housing.

item.title: South Heywood’s 1,000-home masterplan: when will the promised community facilities arrive?
item.description: South Heywood combines an ambition for 1,000 homes with employment development and new community facilities. Russell LDP’s masterplan describes a primary school, local centre, sports pitches, play areas and a 2.2-kilometre link road. Its original hybrid permission dates from March 2020.

item.title: Stakehill’s revised 1,300-home proposal raises questions over affordability and transport
item.description: Barratt is preparing a revised neighbourhood at Stakehill with around 1,300 homes. Its consultation proposes 15% affordable housing: approximately 195 homes if the final total remains 1,300. The remaining tenure detail and actual prices have not been established.

item.title: Station Gardens turns former retail land into 81 homes, but the final tenure mix needs to be public
item.description: Station Gardens is an 81-home development on former Central Retail Park land, delivered through Rochdale Development Agency with Willmott Dixon as contractor. Its announced funding includes £15 million from the Community Regeneration Partnerships Fund, with completion expected in early 2028.

item.title: Trows Farm’s 445 market homes put the spotlight on off-site affordable housing
item.description: The approved Trows Farm scheme is reported as 445 market homes, with an initial £3.75 million contribution towards affordable housing rather than affordable properties within the development. The proposal is smaller than the strategic allocation and those two totals must not be added together.

item.title: Trub Farm’s 158 affordable homes could offer Castleton both rented homes and ownership
item.description: Trub Farm is intended to deliver 158 affordable homes through MCI Developments and Legal & General Affordable Homes. Reported plans comprise 48 apartments and 110 houses, with homes for social rent and shared ownership.

item.title: Wildhouse Meadows’ 47 homes show the gap between housing supply and low-cost housing
item.description: Lancet Homes markets Wildhouse Meadows as a 47-home development in Milnrow. Its current sales page lists three-, four- and five-bedroom houses, with advertised prices from £376,950 and selected larger homes priced substantially higher.

item.title: Nominations Open for Springhill Hospice’s 2026 Man of Rochdale Award
item.description: Springhill Hospice invites nominations for the 2026 Man of Rochdale Award, recognising local heroes who have made significant contributions to the community. The award ceremony will take place later this year.

item.title: Rochdale pupils learn about online safety at Milnrow Crucial Crew
item.description: Year 6 pupils from schools across the Rochdale area have taken part in police-led talks about social media safety and cyberbullying at Milnrow Cricket Club.

item.title: Morning Briefing: Wednesday 14 October 2026
item.description: 11 new stories in the Rochdale borough since yesterday evening.

item.title: Rochdale Borough Council Publishes Budget Report for 2026/27 to 2028/29
item.description: Rochdale Borough Council has published its Budget Report and Medium Term Financial Strategy, outlining financial plans and priorities for the next three years.

item.title: Hollingworth Lake to host Wave of Light walk remembering babies and children
item.description: Families affected by baby or child loss are invited to meet at Hollingworth Lake's beach at 6.30pm on Thursday 15 October for a remembrance walk and 7pm candle-lighting, with bereavement charities and helplines available for support.

item.title: From air traffic control to author: Ramsbottom retiree supports dementia charity
item.description: After 36 years working in air traffic control engineering, Ramsbottom resident Ged has published his debut novel Forget Me Not, with profits going to Alzheimer’s Society and around £700 raised so far.

item.title: Spudbros Opens New Location at EG Station on Manchester Road in Rochdale
item.description: Jacket potato fans in Rochdale welcomed the opening of Spudbros at EG Station on Manchester Road, with the first 100 customers receiving a free meal.

item.title: Rochdale October half-term 2026: school dates and free family activities
item.description: The council's recommended half-term runs from 26 to 30 October. Here are verified free activities at Rochdale Town Hall, Wardle Library and local family hubs, plus what parents should check before travelling.

item.title: Rochdale to Host Ignite Fire Festival Ahead of Christmas Lights Switch-On
item.description: The Ignite Fire Festival will return to Rochdale from November 20 to 22, featuring a new immersive trail and spectacular fire displays.

item.title: Canine Country Club in Rochdale Launches New Classes After Passing Licence Inspection
item.description: Canine Country Club has introduced new puppy sessions and enrichment classes following a successful animal activities licence inspection, enhancing its services for local dog owners.

item.title: Delays on Rochdale East Didsbury Line Due to Track Obstruction
item.description: Tram services on the Rochdale East Didsbury line are delayed following an obstruction on the tracks, with further disruptions across the network due to a road traffic collision.

item.title: Rochdale’s takeaway winning streak continues as Tandoori Flames takes North West title
item.description: Littleborough’s Tandoori Flames is the latest Rochdale borough business to take a regional ARTA title, following wins for River Beal in Milnrow and Wild Ginger in Littleborough last year.

item.title: Rossendale RUFC Defeats Rochdale in Local Derby
item.description: Rossendale RUFC secured a victory over Rochdale in a closely contested local derby, overcoming an early setback to win the match last weekend.

item.title: Breaking news: Rochdale Daily reaches 86,000 readers in 30 days — thank you, Rochdale
item.description: Rochdale Daily is celebrating 86,000 readers in the last 30 days, thanking the borough for its support and setting an ambitious goal of reaching 200,000 readers by November.

item.title: Queues form from 7.20am as SpudBros Express opens in Rochdale
item.description: Early customers queued from around 7.20am for the new SpudBros Express outlet on Manchester New Road, with the first 100 customers promised a free loaded jacket potato at its midday launch.

item.title: Rochdale Sleep Out raises almost £10,000 as organisers make final appeal
item.description: Supporters spent the night outdoors at the Crown Oil Arena for Petrus Community and Rochdale AFC Community Trust, with the annual charity Sleep Out now close to its £10,000 fundraising milestone.

item.title: Finalists Announced for Rochdale Business Awards 2026
item.description: The finalists for the Rochdale Business Awards 2026 have been revealed, with winners set to be announced at a ceremony on 13 November at Rochdale Town Hall.

item.title: Rochdale Sixth Form College Students Disciplined for Ranking Looks in Controversial Online Group
item.description: Students at Rochdale Sixth Form College have faced disciplinary action after creating a Microsoft Teams group that encouraged members to rank their physical attractiveness, with rules enforced by a self-styled 'Founding Father'.
